---
title: "Datasets"
format: html
---

The toolbox uses external gridded datasets through HydroMT catalogs.
The project chooses a catalog and source names; the source files themselves are not distributed with the workflow code.
The table describes roles rather than prescribing a universally best source.

| Data role | Sources represented in the supplied catalog and templates | Effect on the assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Basin hydrography | MERIT Hydro and basin index | Delineation, drainage structure, river network, and output-location placement |
| Model land surface | VITO land cover, MODIS leaf area index, SoilGrids, and river data | Spatial Wflow-SBM parameters and simulated runoff processes |
| Waterbodies and glaciers | HydroLakes, reservoir inventories, and the Randolph Glacier Inventory when configured | Representation of lakes, reservoirs, and glacier processes where relevant |
| Historical meteorology | ERA5 daily forcing; CHIRPS precipitation as a candidate or selected precipitation source | Historical model run and conditioning of weather generation |
| Future climate context | CMIP6 model, scenario, member, and horizon selections | Temperature and precipitation change-factor overlay only |
| Local evaluation | Optional observed daily series at configured output locations | Evidence about historical model performance |

The named sources reflect the supplied [project template](https://github.com/tanerumit/blueearth_cst/blob/main/config/templates/project_config.template.yml), [data catalog](https://github.com/tanerumit/blueearth_cst/blob/main/config/catalogs/deltares_data.yml), and [projection template](https://github.com/tanerumit/blueearth_cst/blob/main/config/templates/project_config.analyze_projections.template.yml).
Catalog entries point to data that must be accessible to the project; their presence in a YAML file does not establish that a dataset is installed or suitable for a basin.

## Choosing and substituting sources

The historical source affects both the reference simulation and the weather generator's baseline statistics.
WF0 can compare available climate variables across candidates before selection.
CHIRPS provides precipitation; when chosen for the full pipeline, the climate store is supplemented with ERA5 variables needed by model building and weather generation.
Inspect the extracted record's coverage, missing values, units, and spatial behavior rather than treating structural readiness as scientific validation.

Changing hydrography can move the basin boundary, river cells, and snapped output points.
Changing land cover, vegetation, or soil sources changes model parameters and may alter simulated response even with identical weather.
Changing the CMIP6 ensemble or windows changes the plausibility overlay, not the weather collection already generated.
Record the catalog, source names, versions, temporal windows, and any local observations when comparing assessments.
